sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.35,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 30.8.2015 at about 3.15 p.m. the petitioner was going towards Mulabagal from his village Kappalamadugu by riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-L-4153 slowly,
cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Narasimhatheertha cross, on four lane highway of Bengaluru- Chennai NH-75 road,
at that time one Verna car bearing No.AP-26- AM-6556 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital,
Kolar, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 33 years, Heavy Transport Vehicle driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement, so the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken as not filed.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.
AP-26-AM- 6556 and its validity.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.
134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the petitioner was solely responsible for the cause of accident.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556 on 30.8.2015 at about 3.15 p.m. near Narasimhathreertha cross, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 to Ex.P15.
8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined Manager, Jalappa hospital, Kolar and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 9.
Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagakumar as PW2, who has assessed 58.4% of whole body disability.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P5 such as FIR with complaint,
Spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.

On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by Chand Pasha, Son of Salar Sab on 31.8.2015.
So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Mulabagal Police in Cr. No.185/2015 against the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
On perusal of Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborate the evidence of PW1.
Ex.P3 is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to both the vehicles and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex. P12
Ex . P4
is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.

The respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the car and in police intimation and MLC record the vehicle number is not mentioned.
To substantiate the said fact, the respondent No.2 has examined Manager of Jalappa Hospital, Tamka as RW1.
He has produced the documents marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 such as authorization letter, police intimation and MLC extract.
On perusal of the same, it shows the alleged H/o RTA on 30.8.2015 at about 3.30 p.m. near Mulbagal where he was hit by a car.
But on perusal of complaint it shows that the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26- AM-6556 has drove his vehicle and dashed against the motor cycle.
In the charge sheet also I.O. has charge sheeted against the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556.

if the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556 has not caused the accident, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the vehicle would have contested the case by filing the written statement,
moreover he has challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the car.
But he has not do so.
From this it is clear that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556.
On the other hand, petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 30.8.2015 at about 3.15 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital,
Tamka, Kolar wherein he took the treatment as inpatient.
The doctor is of the opinion that the injury Nos. 1 to 5 are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge card marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.8.2015 to 29.10.2015 and underwent debridement and external fixator application for left elbow and ORIF with recon nailing for left femur, ORIF with LCP plating of right distal femur was done on 21.9.2015 and ORIF with K wire fixation for inter condylar fracture humerus and TBW for olecranon fracture.
21. PW2- Dr.Nagakumar has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained above said injuries and underwent surgeries.

He has produced OPD card, disability evaluation form, inpatient records, X-rays with CD marked at Ex.P11 to Ex.P15.
22.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 & PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.80,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
23. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 33 years, Heavy transport vehicle driver and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But he has not produced pertains to his avocation and income.
In the absence of the documents pertains to his avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner and the year of accident, if notional income of Rs.6,500/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.
the petitioner has produced discharge summaries marked at Ex.P6 and Ex.P6, which shows that he was admitted from 30.8.2015 to 29.10.2015 and again he was admitted from 17.11.2015 to 24.11.2015.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries; he might have taken rest and treatment at least for four months.
Therefore, four months income comes to Rs.26,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
24. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.2,52,027/-.

On perusal of cross-examination of PW1, the counsel for the respondent No.2 has suggested that at Ex.P10 at Sl.No.1 it shows five pages, but instead of five pages, the petitioner has produced two pages.
For which the petitioner has stated that rest of the pages were lost.
So, the petitioner has not produced entire pages to show that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

Moreover,
if the remaining pages were lost, at least he tried to examine the author of the document, but he has not do so.
So part of the document cannot be considered.
Therefore, after deducting the said amount of Rs.1,35,645/- from the amount of Rs.2,52,027/- it comes to Rs.1,16,382/-.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,16,382/- towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years, Heavy Transport Vehicle driver and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he is completely bedridden, and lost his earnings.

His both lower limbs and left upper limb have been very grievous injured, except driving he do not know any other work which he is disabled to do The petitioner has produced photographs and CD marked at Ex.P9 and Ex.P9(a).
26. To prove the age, the petitioner has produced driving license marked at Ex.P8.
On perusal of the same the date of birth of the petitioner was mentioned as 4.12.1979.
The accident occurred on 30.8.2015.
So, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 35 years.
So, same is considered as the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident 27.

PW2-Dr.Naga Kumar has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained Traumatic brain injury, Open Type IIIIA inter condylar fracture of left humerus (left arm), left olecranon (Left elbow) fracture, segmental fracture of left femur (left thigh) , Intra articular distal 1/3rd femur fracture right side (right thigh) and left 5th metatarsal (toe) fracture and underwent surgeries.
He has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.

According to him, the petitioner has 58.4%
of whole body disability.

So, considering the evidence of PW2 and the cross- examination and the age and avocation of the petitioner and relative disability, if 40% is considered as whole body of disability of the petitioner, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner age is already considered as 35 years the multiplier applicable to this age is 16.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.4,99,200/- under the head of loss of future earning.
29. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained fractures.
So his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of amenities.

30. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient from discharge card marked at Ex.P6 and Ex.P6, which shows that he was admitted from 30.8.2015 to 29.10.2015 and again from 17.11.2015 to 24.11.2015 and also took the treatment as outpatient.

So,
one must attend him during the above said period.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.

31 PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner requires surgeries for removal of implants, left femur bone grafting and exchange nailing for left femur, K-wire removal and realignment of the fracture of distal end of humerus and to reduce joint with appropriate implant or total elbow orthroplasty which costs of Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/-, Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- and Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.1,50,000/-.

So,
relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
under this head.

 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs. 80,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 26,000-00 and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,16,382-00 4. Loss of future income Rs. 4,99,200-00 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 20,000-00
6. Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 50,000-00 conveyance charges 7.
Future medication Rs. 1,00,000-00 Total Rs.8,91,582-00 33.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.AP-26-AM-6556.
34.

The respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of car bearing No.
AP-26-AM-6556 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,91,582/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized/scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
